title: Cyber Dictionary
summary: A plain-English dictionary of technology and cybersecurity terms, with a library of open data sources, documented incident case studies and printable editions, built for quick lookups on the job.

narrative.problem: The terms, protocols, attacks and frameworks that come up on the job are scattered across long references, and open data sources are hard to wire into a project without knowing which API, key requirement and cost each one involves.
narrative.decision: Keeps all content in plain data files (terms.js, library.js and Markdown case studies) that the site, the build-time checks and the generated PDF books all read, so the printed editions cannot drift from the website.
narrative.tradeoff: Each definition is held to one or two sentences for quick lookups, which costs precision; with no framework or build step, entries are edited by appending objects to arrays by hand.
narrative.limitation: A reference rather than a study: definitions are brief and in the CoLab's own wording, the published counts are snapshots that change with each commit, and links refused by bot protection are recorded as not verified.
